 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Jerry Jones is facing criticism after the Dallas Cowboys stripped defensive coordinator Christian Parker of his play-calling responsibilities, with former receiver Jesse Holley questioning the decision and its impact on the coaching staff. 
 The change follows Dallas' disappointing 46-40 defeat to the San Francisco 49ers, who piled up 584 total yards and scored three touchdowns of at least 66 yards.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Owner and general manager Jones had already acknowledged that the Cowboys were considering changes to Parker's responsibilities before Mike Pettine was handed control of the defensive play-calling.
 Jesse Holley questions Jerry Jones' decision to take duties away from Christian Parker
 Speaking on the DLLS Cowboys podcast, Holley did not hold back when discussing the decision, describing it as "n**** work".
 He said: "This is n**** work. This is some very, very disgusting, despicable, deplorable, filthy work. If I'm a player in that locker room, who do I trust? Who do I answer to? Do I answer to Mike Pettine? Will he be the DC next year, or won't he?"
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Holley believes the change could create confusion within the locker room, particularly with Parker retaining his defensive coordinator title despite losing control of the play-calling.
 He also questioned whether the move could signal the beginning of the end of Parker's time in Dallas.
 "History says, when you lose your play-calling duties, especially the defensive coordinator in the middle of the season, you lose your job at the end of it," Holley added.
 The former Cowboys receiver was also unhappy with how publicly the organisation handled the situation, arguing that it could undermine Parker's authority.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Pettine's appointment is particularly notable given their previous relationship. He originally hired Parker as a defensive quality control coach with the Green Bay Packers in 2019 before both eventually arrived in Dallas.
 However, head coach Brian Schottenheimer has publicly backed Parker and insisted he remains central to the team's plans.
 "Christian Parker is still our defensive coordinator," Schottenheimer said. "He's a critical piece of what we're trying to do as we search for answers and solutions. I think he has an incredibly bright future, not just this year, but beyond with us."
 Pettine will take charge of the defensive play-calling against the Tennessee Titans. The Cowboys will be hoping the change produces an immediate improvement, while Parker's role within the coaching staff remains under scrutiny.
